A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CitePretrainBench and Active Indexing work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original Qwen experiments on four citation QA tasks, scaling and memorization analyses, and appendix experiments on identifiers, Wikipedia tasks, and augmentation generators.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds GPT-4.1 baseline results and experiments comparing internal, external, and hybrid citations across retrieval conditions.

M1.justification: The original forward/backward Active Indexing procedure remains unchanged. However, Section 5.4 and Appendix C.2 add substantial retrieval integration procedures: Hybrid Joint trains on retrieved-document inputs and assesses document sufficiency, while Hybrid Fallback routes an abstaining RAG system to Hybrid Joint. v1 discussed hybridization only as future work.

E1.justification: Dataset membership remains unchanged, including the appendix TriviaQA and HotpotQA tasks. Section 5.4 nevertheless substantially extends test scenarios across the four main QA datasets by supplying retrieved evidence of varying quality, adding evidence-conditioned and noisy-retrieval environments to the earlier closed-book evaluation.

E2.justification: v2 adds GPT-4.1 as an evaluated comparator on ASQA, ELI5, and SciQAG, with no RepliQA results reported. Section 5.4 adds comparisons among Internal Only, External Only RAG, Hybrid Joint, Hybrid Fallback, and Hybrid Oracle. Original main-table comparators remain, although the separate forward/backward/combined scaling comparison is removed.

E3.justification: New protocols mix sparse and dense top-five retrieval results across six proportions and report correctness plus citation F1. Hybrid training creates sparse-context and dense-context instances per question. GPT-4.1 uses three-shot prompting without constrained citation decoding. These are added experimental designs; the retained experiments' splits and main training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a substantial retrieval-quality robustness study comparing internal, external, and hybrid strategies. It removes v1 Figure 2's separate forward/backward/combined augmentation scaling analysis. The active-versus-passive scaling comparison, memorization analysis, and appendix identifier, error, qualitative-example, and generator-quality analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, evaluation seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars. v2 continues the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: All 168 original Qwen main-table values and retained appendix-table results match. v2 adds GPT-4.1 results, including ASQA correctness/citation precision of 52.7/23.0, and the retrieval-quality curves in Figure 3; directional scaling results disappear. These are added or removed results, not improved retained scores. Figure 3's internal-only ASQA correctness near 18 is unexplained relative to Table 1's 7B ActIdx value of 27.6.

T1.justification: The corpus, statement/citation, and augmentation formalizations retain the same mathematical substance. The rewritten problem formulation restates the existing mappings; no new theorem, proof, derivation, or substantive formal assumption is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion add a central claim that internal citations improve robustness to retrieval noise through combination with external citations. The introduction further claims hybrid superiority across conditions and highlights proprietary models' citation failures despite strong answer correctness. The original benchmark and Active Indexing contribution claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 develops a substantive account of applicability under retrieval failures versus strong external evidence, and interprets the oracle gap as an integration limitation. It also attributes GPT-4.1's citation failures to missing identifier associations and adds future work on strengthening existing bindings. v1's scalability, synthetic-data, and automatic-evaluation limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix C.2 adds hybrid training and abstention-routing details, and the release promise now specifies publication. Conversely, the corpus-statistics table and the 66M/76M RepliQA augmentation breakdown and subsampling explanation disappear. Existing main hyperparameters, hardware, training-time disclosures, and augmentation prompts are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 moves and expands the existing generative-retrieval discussion, sharpening the distinction from closed-book citation. Appendix B substantially expands coverage of fine-grained external attribution and tracing methods, including SEMQA, LongCite, TokenShapley, OLMoTrace, and RapidIn. These are substantive positioning additions beyond the citation-style conversion.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, problem formulation, dataset description, and Section 5.3 undergo extensive rewriting and condensation. The two scaling discussions are consolidated, the reproducibility statement expands, acknowledgments disappear, and an LLM-writing disclosure appendix is added.

P2.justification: v2 globally changes the title/abstract presentation, text area, running headers, heading styling, and table-caption placement. The main table gains a GPT-4.1 row; the corpus table and directional scaling figure disappear; an eight-panel retrieval figure is added. v1 Figure 3 is retained unchanged as v2 Figure 2.

improvement.justification: The new retrieval-quality study gives empirical substance to hybridization, which v1 presented as future work, and the broader comparisons and related work improve practical context. Gains are limited by removing directional scaling evidence and corpus statistics. The new evidence also needs tighter qualification: External Only exceeds both practical hybrids on ELI5 citation F1 under stronger retrieval, and Figure 3 leaves the ASQA baseline discrepancy unexplained.
